name: Shormann Math
line: Shormann Math teaches by lecture and tests at set points. In AMP, assessment and teaching happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs Shormann Math: Shormann teaches by recorded lecture and tests at set points. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: Shormann Math teaches each lesson by recorded lecture, then practice, in a fixed order, with a quiz every fourth lesson and a cumulative exam every 25 [2][3]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer is checked and explained at once, updates the learner's level and sets the next problem.

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. Shormann Math uses a placement test to choose the course [5]. Inside the course every student works the same lessons in the same order, with a timed quiz every fourth lesson and a cumulative exam every 25 lessons [2][3].

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a film where there is one, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In Shormann Math the unit is the lesson. It opens with flashcards of rules and definitions and a recorded whiteboard lecture by Dr. Shormann, during which the student works each example. The practice set comes after [2][3]. Across 55 studies, worked examples improve performance in math [9].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer, AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. Shormann Math grades the typed answers automatically. A student gets up to four attempts on each problem, with points taken off for each miss, and then video and PDF solutions open [2]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in mixed ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [10].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP an answer given after a hint or a lesson is marked as helped. A skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once, and repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on, on one map from counting through precalculus. In Shormann Math a grade is weighted points across practice, quizzes and exams [2][3]. The first 25 lessons of each course review and introduce prerequisite skills, the same for every student [3].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. Each learner's own answers decide when a skill is due back. Shormann Math reviews in the Saxon manner: a concept returns in several later practice sets, then on a timed quiz and a quarterly exam [3]. The course sets that order, the same for every student [2]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later on the researchers' own test, against 38% for practice in blocks [8].

rows.range: Prealgebra, for grade 7 and up, through Calculus 2, as separate courses, with geometry woven into the algebra courses [1][4].
rows.start: A placement test, posted by the maker, chooses the course. The course then runs in a fixed order [5][2].
rows.teaching: Recorded whiteboard lectures by Dr. Shormann and a printable eTextbook. Each problem links to a similar worked example [2][3].
rows.next: The next lesson in the course's fixed order, the same for every student. The family sets the pace [2].
rows.mastery: Weighted points for practice, quizzes and exams. Up to four tries per problem, with points off for each miss [2][3].
rows.review: In the Saxon manner: a concept returns in later practice sets, a timed quiz and a quarterly exam, on the course's schedule [3].
rows.print: A printable eTextbook and teacher's guide, the same for every student [1][2].
rows.adult: Reads the teacher's guide, views the gradebook, and can request grade changes or reset assignments. The course is built for independent work [1][2][3].
rows.reports: Automatic grades and weighted course grades in a parent gradebook [1][2].
rows.evidence: None found on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [1][6][7].

theirs: Shormann Math comes from DIVE Interactive Education, created by Dr. Shormann [1][5]. It is a line of self-paced online courses: Prealgebra, Algebra 1 and Algebra 2 with integrated geometry, Precalculus with Trigonometry, Calculus 1 and Calculus 2 [1]. The method is Saxon's incremental approach with geometry woven in [1], taught from a Christian worldview [3].

Each course is a fixed sequence of lessons [2]. A lesson opens with digital flashcards of rules and definitions, then a recorded whiteboard lecture by Dr. Shormann, during which the student pauses to solve each example [2][3]. Then come practice problems, worked on paper with the answers typed online and graded automatically. A short timed quiz comes every fourth lesson, and a cumulative exam every 25 lessons [2][3].
credit: One teacher explains every lesson, and the student works each example with him [2][3].
Old topics keep returning in later practice sets, quizzes and exams, in the Saxon manner [3].
Each practice problem links to a similar worked example and the lecture that taught it [2].

theirs: We found no outcome study of Shormann Math on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [1][5][6][7].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, in mixed ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect (0.49), against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [10]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later on the researchers' own test, against 38% for practice in blocks [8]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and the code is public.

them: You want one teacher's recorded lecture for each lesson, followed by a set of practice problems.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want every answer checked and explained the moment it is given.
You want a hint, a lesson and the worked answer at every problem.
You want review timed to what your learner has learned and when.
Your learner is at different levels in different parts of math.

questions.question: How is AMP different from Shormann Math?
questions.answer: Shormann Math teaches each lesson by recorded lecture, then practice, with quizzes and exams at set points in a fixed order [2][3]. AMP has no separate test: every answer is checked and explained at once and sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does Shormann Math work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of Shormann Math on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [1][6][7].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. AMP places a learner from their first answers, whatever else they use.
